answer_sql:
SELECT
  reading,
  country,
  SUM(net_amount) AS net_revenue
FROM (
  SELECT
    'shop' AS reading,
    c.country_name AS country,
    l.net_amount
  FROM contoso_served.v_contoso5_sales_line AS l
  JOIN contoso_served.dim_store AS s
    ON l.store_key = s.store_key
  JOIN contoso_served.dim_country AS c
    ON s.country_code = c.country_code
  WHERE
    c.country_name IN ('Germany', 'France')
  UNION ALL
  SELECT
    'buyer' AS reading,
    c.country_name AS country,
    l.net_amount
  FROM contoso_served.v_contoso5_sales_line AS l
  JOIN contoso_served.dim_customer AS cu
    ON l.customer_key = cu.customer_key
  JOIN contoso_served.dim_country AS c
    ON cu.country_code = c.country_code
  WHERE
    c.country_name IN ('Germany', 'France')
) AS t
GROUP BY
  reading,
  country
ORDER BY
  reading,
  country

One row is one country under one meaning of "in". What is NOT in these figures: no returns and no tax are netted off, because this bundle records neither, so "net" means after discount and nothing more; no currency conversion, because net_amount is already USD on every line whatever currency the sale was transacted in; no period restriction; no other country, so these do not sum to any company total (all countries and both channels together are 218,814,471.66). value:
Germany is well ahead of France — but by how much depends on one thing you did not say, so tell me which you meant and the pair of figures is ready either way: by "in Germany" and "in France", do you mean where the customer lives, or where the shop stands?

• WHERE OUR CUSTOMERS LIVE — web orders included: Germany 24,638,830.18, France 6,674,724.85
• WHERE OUR SHOPS STAND — walk-in sales only, because the web shop stands in no country: Germany 14,382,768.44, France 3,722,647.45

There is no country recorded on a sale itself, which is why this has to be asked rather than assumed — a sale reaches a country either through the shop that rang it up or through the buyer who placed it.

What the choice does NOT change: Germany leads France either way, and by much the same multiple — 3.7x on the customer reading, 3.9x on the shop reading. So if the comparison is what you are after, you have it already. The entire difference between the two readings is web-shop revenue, 10,256,061.74 for Germany and 2,952,077.40 for France; the walk-in figures are identical under both readings, because every sale in a German or French shop was made by a customer registered in that same country.

All four figures are USD after discount, over every order from 2016-05-18 to 2025-12-31, since you named no period.

Two populations, both reported, neither chosen. SHOP reading: the 18,050 sales lines whose selling store carries country code DE or FR (Germany 14,190 lines, France 3,860) — walk-in only in effect, because the one online store carries the '--' sentinel rather than a country and so matches neither name. BUYER reading: the 32,650 sales lines whose customer is registered in DE or FR (Germany 25,552, France 7,098) — walk-in and web together. Neither is period-restricted: all time, order dates 2016-05-18 to 2025-12-31, per order.default.an_unscoped_question_covers_all_time. Neither applies a channel predicate, because store.resolution.the_channel_is_the_location_sentinel scopes its `physical` default with `applies: subject` and this question's subject is a measure. The '--' sentinel falls outside both by construction, per country.exclusion.sentinel_is_not_a_country. The site-country path is not a third population — measured 0 disagreements over all 223,974 lines, it returns the shop figures exactly.

value.sql:
SELECT
  reading,
  country,
  SUM(net_amount) AS net_revenue
FROM (
  SELECT
    'shop' AS reading,
    c.country_name AS country,
    l.net_amount
  FROM contoso_served.v_contoso5_sales_line AS l
  JOIN contoso_served.dim_store AS s
    ON l.store_key = s.store_key
  JOIN contoso_served.dim_country AS c
    ON s.country_code = c.country_code
  WHERE
    c.country_name IN ('Germany', 'France')
  UNION ALL
  SELECT
    'buyer' AS reading,
    c.country_name AS country,
    l.net_amount
  FROM contoso_served.v_contoso5_sales_line AS l
  JOIN contoso_served.dim_customer AS cu
    ON l.customer_key = cu.customer_key
  JOIN contoso_served.dim_country AS c
    ON cu.country_code = c.country_code
  WHERE
    c.country_name IN ('Germany', 'France')
) AS t
GROUP BY
  reading,
  country
ORDER BY
  reading,
  country
value.means: The money Contoso actually charged, after discount, in USD, over every order placed between 2016-05-18 and 2025-12-31 — totalled for each of the two countries under each of the two meanings of "in". Where the buyer lives: Germany 24,638,830.18, France 6,674,724.85. Where the shop stands: Germany 14,382,768.44, France 3,722,647.45. Four figures, no returns or tax netted off because this bundle records neither; "net" here means after discount and nothing else.

value.means: These four rows are the money Contoso actually charged, after discount, in USD, totalled for Germany and for France over the full ten years of orders — each country costed twice, once by where the shop stood and once by where the buyer lived. One row is one country under one meaning of "in". What is NOT in these figures: no returns and no tax are netted off, because this bundle records neither, so "net" means after discount and nothing more; no currency conversion, because net_amount is already USD on every line whatever currency the sale was transacted in; no period restriction; no other country, so these do not sum to any company total (all countries and both channels together are 218,814,471.66). And the two readings are never added or averaged, which would count every German walk-in sale twice.
